label: cor:local
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:local}
Consider the model \eqref{eq:model}, and let $s$ and $t$ lie in a common edge. Under the Mat'ern model the field is $m$ times mean square differentiable along that edge if and only if $
u>m$. Its sample paths there have fractal index $2
u$ for $
u<1$ under the Mat'ern model, and $\alpha$ under the powered exponential and generalized Cauchy models.

label: ex:st
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:st}
A concrete choice is $\eta(r)=\exp(-c\,r^{\gamma})$, with $c>0$ and $0<\gamma\leq1$, together with $\psi(r)=\{1+(r/b^{2})^{\alpha}\}^{\beta}$, with $b>0$,
$0<\alpha\leq1$ and $0<\beta\leq1$. Both
appear in Tables 1 and 2 of \cite{gneiting2002nonseparable}. They give
$$ C\big((s,u),(t,w)\big) \;=\; \frac{\sigma^2}
{[1+\{h_\kappa(s,t)/b\}^{2\alpha}]^{\beta/2}}\,
\exp\!\left(-\,\frac{c\,|u-w|^{2\gamma}}
{[1+\{h_\kappa(s,t)/b\}^{2\alpha}]^{\beta\gamma}}\right),$$
which is a covariance function on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}$ for every metric tree. Setting
$u=w$ gives the generalized Cauchy correlation of Table \ref{tab:phi} in the spatial argument, and setting $s=t$
gives the powered exponential correlation in time. The parameter $\beta$
governs the interaction between the two arguments, and the limiting value $\beta=0$ gives the
separable model, the product of those two correlations.

title: Proof
body_md:
Every path from $\xi_{j}$ to a point of $P$
passes through $m_j(s,t)$, so that $d(\xi_{j},s)=d(\xi_{j},m_j(s,t))+p_j(s,t)$ and
$d(\xi_{j},t)=d(\xi_{j},m_j(s,t))+p_j(t,s)$. Subtracting, and using $p_j(s,t)+p_j(t,s)=d(s,t)$,
\[
d(\xi_{j},s) - d(\xi_{j},t) = p_j(s,t) - p_j(t,s) = \{2x_j(s,t)-1\}\,d(s,t) .
\]
Squaring, averaging over $j=1,\hdots,\kappa$ and using \eqref{eq:h},
$h_\kappa^2(s,t)=d^2(s,t)\kappa^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^\kappa\{2x_j(s,t)-1\}^2$, which is \eqref{eq:xsq} because
$(2x-1)^2=1-4x(1-x)$.
\hfill$\square$
